verdict.headline: Iran's Hormuz draft spikes oil and snaps the Dow's five-day winning streak
verdict.label: HOLD — SPX 7,710 (−0.18%); Nasdaq 26,348 (−0.06%); Dow 53,885 (−0.85%, 5-day streak ends); UWMC −33%; APP −21%; HONA −20%; SPCX +5% despite 911M lockup; WTI $77.29 (+2.8%); Brent $82.49 (+3.8%); AH: TTD −26%, NET +17%, TWLO +15.7%, ABNB +8%; 30Y 5.20% sole breach; 1-of-6 regime; NFP Friday 8:30 AM ET
verdict.rationale_short: Iran's state media published a restrictive Hormuz draft banning US and Israeli ships and imposing 20% cargo penalties on violators — reversing three sessions of oil relief and sending WTI up 2.8% to $77.29 ($1.71 from the $79 formal trigger) and Brent up 3.8% to $82.49 ($2.51 from $85). The 10Y yield rose 6bps to 4.68% on the oil surge, and the Dow shed 0.85% (−464 pts), ending its five-day winning streak — but SPX lost only 0.18% and Nasdaq just 0.06%, showing tech resilience held the broader index. Intraday earnings carnage was severe: UWM Holdings (UWMC) collapsed 33% after announcing its first-ever dividend suspension and a Q2 net loss of $452M; AppLovin (APP) fell 21% to $331.57 on a Q2 revenue miss ($1.92B vs $1.94B est, +53% YoY) with FCF compressing to $863M vs $1.29B expected; Honeywell Aerospace (HONA) slid 20% after slashing its full-year organic growth outlook to 4–5% from 7–9%. SPCX bucked the lockup-expiry selloff: 911M shares unlocked, more than doubling the float, and the stock still closed up roughly 5% to ~$113 as institutional buyers absorbed supply at the $108 base set Wednesday. After the close, the signal split: Trade Desk (TTD) crashed 26% on revenue growth decelerating to just 3% YoY with a full C-suite reset (CFO, CMO, chief commercial officer all replaced) — a deeper ad-tech implosion than APP's miss. Countering that: Cloudflare (NET) +17%, Twilio (TWLO) +15.7%, and Airbnb (ABNB) +8% all beat on top and bottom lines with raised guidance, setting up a constructive cloud/travel open Friday. September hike odds sit near 52% heading into NFP (consensus 80–88K; ADP 44K argues downside). Below 80K: September falls below 45%, Kashkari isolated, 30Y path to 5.00% opens. Above 130K: September crosses 70%, second regime breach triggers, and Brent at $82.49 means oil could breach simultaneously.

watchlist_mentions.note: AH −26% after revenue growth decelerated to just 3% YoY — far below the ~20%+ pace the stock had priced in. Simultaneously replaced CFO, CMO, and chief commercial officer. This is a deeper ad-tech implosion than APP's −21% during the regular session; the C-suite reset signals management recognizes the problem is structural, not a one-quarter noise trade. The TTD move arriving the same night as APP's miss confirms ad-tech as the cycle's weak point.

First revenue miss in multiple quarters for a stock pricing near-perfection in AI ad-tech. Analyst downgrade notes Friday morning set the re-entry zone.

Q3 Starlink profitability (~October) is the key catalyst; December expiry is the next supply event.

trade_setups.thesis: 30Y at 5.20% is the sole formal breach, 20bps above 5.00%. September hike odds at 52% are 18 points from the 70% trigger. Friday's NFP (8:30 AM ET; consensus 80–88K; ADP 44K points to downside) is the week's remaining independent variable. Below 80K: September falls below 45%, Kashkari isolated, 30Y has path toward 5.00%, regime moves to 0-of-6. Above 130K: September approaches 70%, second breach triggers, and with Brent at $82.49, oil breaches could arrive simultaneously.
trade_setups.entry: Binary event. 5.00% and 5.28% are the formal 30Y clearing levels on either side of current 5.20%.
trade_setups.invalidation: Khamenei approves the restrictive Hormuz draft before 8:30 AM ET Friday, pushing Brent above $85 and repricing September odds independent of NFP.
trade_setups.horizon: 24 hours through NFP Aug 7; medium-term through CPI Aug 13

trade_setups.thesis: Three sessions of oil-deflation momentum reversed on a single draft document. Brent $82.49 is $2.51 from the $85 trigger; WTI $77.29 is $1.71 from $79. Khamenei's response to the restrictive draft is the binary: approval activates two oil regime thresholds simultaneously. A rejection returns oil toward $74, re-opening the rate-relief and equity-momentum setup that Tuesday through Wednesday had built.
trade_setups.entry: Brent $85 and WTI $79 are the formal trigger levels. The week's 11% oil decline has been partially recaptured (3–4%); Khamenei's response resolves the direction.
trade_setups.invalidation: Khamenei rejects the draft or proposes material concessions bringing the framework closer to a full reopening; Brent falls back below $79.
trade_setups.horizon: 24–72 hours for diplomatic resolution; immediate market transmission on any approval

trade_setups.asset: Ad-tech collapse — TTD + APP as pattern
trade_setups.thesis: Trade Desk (TTD) −26% AH on 3% revenue growth plus C-suite reset arrived the same night AppLovin (APP) fell 21% during the session on a revenue miss. Two of the largest independent ad-tech platforms printing in consecutive sessions with catastrophic reactions. The shared variable is not one-off execution but structural: programmatic ad budgets are concentrating toward Google/Meta duopoly, leaving pure-play ad-tech platforms fighting for share at declining margins. The pattern may extend to other names with ad-revenue exposure reporting in coming weeks.
trade_setups.entry: No specific level — sector-level pattern forming. The next major ad-tech or DSP print is the confirming data point. MNTN, DV, MGNI are smaller names in the ecosystem that trade directionally with TTD.
trade_setups.invalidation: TTD management provides an off-cycle analyst update citing a one-time budget-timing issue rather than structural revenue deceleration; stock recovers above pre-earnings close within 3 sessions.

bear_case: Iran's restrictive Hormuz draft, if approved by Khamenei before Friday's NFP print, pushes Brent above $85 and WTI above $79 simultaneously — activating two oil regime thresholds that have not been triggered together this cycle. An approval before 8:30 AM ET Friday then collides with an above-consensus NFP (above 130K), removing the labor-softness argument that has kept September hike odds below 70% all week. Three simultaneous breaches — 30Y, Brent, and September hike odds — would represent the broadest regime widening since the Iran escalation peaked in June. The TTD C-suite reset and APP revenue miss in the same 24-hour window, following DDOG −17% and Figma −16.5% on Aug 5, are adding weight to an ad-tech and high-multiple SaaS de-rating that could broaden into the index if NFP disappoints growth expectations. SPX closing below 7,380 on that combination is the level that invalidates this read.
